blocks.text: Condo buildings in Buckingham Heights
Streets, schools and getting around Buckingham Heights

items.t: Buckingham Heights is the detached-house slope east and south-east of Deer Lake in the City of Burnaby, surrounding Buckingham Elementary School (6066 Buckingham Ave) between Deer Lake Park and Royal Oak Avenue, in south-central Burnaby. "Buckingham Heights" is the GVR board sub-area name in the SnapStats GVR report, listed separately from Deer Lake, Deer Lake Place and Upper Deer Lake. The City publishes no street-by-street written boundary for the MLS® sub-area — exact boundary streets: Not verified.

Main streets and edges: Canada Way along the north side, Sperling Avenue down the park's east side, Buckingham Drive / Buckingham Avenue serving the slope streets, and Royal Oak Avenue along the west side toward Kingsway. Deer Lake Park (6450 Deer Lake Ave) sits directly north-west; Burnaby Hospital (3935 Kincaid St) is north-west across Canada Way; Metrotown is south-west.
Where the condo stock concentrates: nowhere — there is none. The sub-area is effectively all freehold detached housing.

Burnaby community-level context (SnapStats publishes medians at community level only, not for Buckingham Heights): Condos & Townhomes median sale price $686,000, $763/sqft, sale-to-list 98%, 36 days on market in September 2026 — those are Burnaby-wide figures, not this sub-area's.

Transit: there is no SkyTrain station inside Buckingham Heights; Royal Oak Station (Expo Line), to the south-west, is the nearest station named. Specific bus route numbers for the sub-area's streets: Not verified.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Buckingham Heights

items.t: Burnaby zoning — current bylaw: the Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026, No. 14815, was adopted June 9, 2026 and took effect July 1, 2026; the former Zoning Bylaw No. 4742 (1965) is repealed — any source still citing Bylaw 4742 for Burnaby is superseded. Burnaby consolidated its single- and two-family districts into one R1 Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing (SSMUH) District in June 2024: R1 lots may hold 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 units on larger lots, and 6 units on lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop, and lots with two or more primary units may be stratified.

Burnaby 2050 OCP: the Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan, adopted December 9, 2025, replaces the 1998 OCP and takes precedence over older community-plan land use maps where they conflict; the Royal Oak Community Plan covers the plan area west of Buckingham Heights.

blocks.text: Good to know about Buckingham Heights

items.t: The park boardwalk is partly closed into 2027. The section of boardwalk by the Deer Lake boat launch closed September 21, 2026 for a full replacement, with completion scheduled by winter 2027 and a signed detour via Sperling Avenue and Deer Lake Drive adding about five minutes of walking; part of the nearby picnic area is also closed during construction.

The Sperling Avenue edge is a heritage precinct. Sperling Avenue fronting Deer Lake Park, at the sub-area's north-east edge, lies within the Deer Lake Park Heritage Precinct, where the City's heritage register lists early-1900s houses such as the Woodward House at 5195 Sperling Avenue (built 1912) — heritage review can apply to renovations and rebuilds on that edge.
A zero-sale month is normal here, not a warning.
Do not borrow the Deer Lake sub-area's numbers.

The park next door is the city's cultural centre. Deer Lake Park is described by the City as a peaceful natural environment that serves as the cultural centre of the city, connecting the lake, Burnaby Art Gallery, Shadbolt Centre for the Arts, Burnaby Village Museum and Hart House restaurant; it is open dawn to dusk year-round.

There is no mall, recreation centre or SkyTrain inside the sub-area. The confirmed anchors are all at its edges — Metrotown (the city's downtown / regional city centre) south-west, the Bob Prittie Metrotown library branch, Burnaby Hospital across Canada Way, and City Hall at 4949 Canada Way. A City recreation facility inside Buckingham Heights: Not verified.

Streets, schools and getting around Buckingham Heights

items.t: "Buckingham Heights" is the GVR board sub-area name in the SnapStats GVR report for Burnaby, listed separately from Deer Lake, Deer Lake Place and Upper Deer Lake, which border it. The City of Burnaby publishes no street-by-street written boundary for the MLS® sub-area — exact boundary streets: Not verified. The residential area surrounds Buckingham Elementary (6066 Buckingham Ave), between Deer Lake to the north-west and Royal Oak Avenue to the west / south-west, on Buckingham Drive / Buckingham Avenue streets.

Main roads and edges: Canada Way runs along the north side, Sperling Avenue runs down Deer Lake Park's east side, Buckingham Drive / Buckingham Avenue serve the slope streets, and Royal Oak Avenue runs along the west side toward Kingsway. Deer Lake Park (6450 Deer Lake Ave) is directly north-west; Burnaby Hospital (3935 Kincaid St, Fraser Health) is north-west across Canada Way; Metrotown, the city's downtown / regional city centre, is south-west and is this area's main shopping destination — there is no enclosed mall or shopping centre inside the sub-area.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates: nowhere — there is none. The sub-area is effectively all freehold detached housing.
Sub-area median prices by property type: Not verified.
Schools: SD41 (Burnaby) runs K–7 elementary and 8–12 secondary with no middle-school tier.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Buckingham Heights

items.t: Form B diligence (strata purchases): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page.

Burnaby zoning — standing correction applied: the governing bylaw is the Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815, adopted June 9, 2026, in effect July 1, 2026), never the former 1965 No. 4742. The R1 SSMUH District carried into it allows 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 units on larger lots, and 6 units on lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop; lots with two or more primary units may be stratified. The Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan, adopted December 9, 2025, replaces the 1998 OCP and takes precedence over older community-plan maps where they conflict; the Royal Oak Community Plan covers the plan area west of Buckingham Heights. Heritage-precinct and park-edge lots (the Sperling Avenue edge, inside the Deer Lake Park Heritage Precinct) carry extra review — eligibility is confirmed lot by lot.

blocks.text: Good to know about Buckingham Heights

items.t: The boardwalk at the area's doorstep is closed into 2027. The section of boardwalk by the Deer Lake boat launch closed September 21, 2026 for a full replacement, with completion scheduled by winter 2027 and a signed detour via Sperling Avenue and Deer Lake Drive (about five extra minutes of walking); a small section of the nearby picnic area is also closed during construction.
Deer Lake Park is the city's cultural centre, not just a park.

Burnaby replaced its OCP and its zoning bylaw within seven months. The Burnaby 2050 OCP was adopted December 9, 2025 (replacing the 1998 OCP and taking precedence over older community-plan maps), and Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815) was adopted June 9, 2026 and took effect July 1, 2026 — any density or land-use claim for a Buckingham lot sourced to the old OCP or the old bylaw is out of date.

The detached utility bill has a fixed shape here. Burnaby's 2026 residential utility notice covers annual water, annual sewer use, a cross-connection device charge where applicable, and a garbage toter fee; the detached single-family water charge is $652.33, rates carry a 5% discount if paid by the due date, and for single-family homes sewer is billed as a sewer parcel tax on the property tax notice.

City Hall is at the lake, not downtown. Burnaby City Hall is at 4949 Canada Way, north-west of the sub-area at Deer Lake — civic business for this slope is a short drive, and the Bob Prittie Metrotown Branch is the quadrant's public library branch.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Buckingham Heights
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Established-street house lots: detached single-family housing only — the slope streets east and south-east of Deer Lake. A fee-simple lot carries NO strata, NO Form B and NO strata fees.

Lot character: typical lot sizes are not verified at sub-area level — no official source read states them. The only lot-size figures documented are the R1 SSMUH thresholds: 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 units on larger lots, and 6 units on lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop. These are zoning thresholds, not a claim about any existing lot's size; the zone and dimensions of a specific lot are confirmed parcel by parcel.

Historic lot fabric — built stock, not offerings: the Buckingham Drive / Buckingham Avenue streets around Buckingham Elementary hold the core stock, and the Sperling Avenue edge, inside the Deer Lake Park Heritage Precinct, holds heritage-register houses such as the Woodward House at 5195 Sperling Avenue (built 1912). That is the built lot fabric of the area — no lot in it is documented as a bare-land offering.

Serviced position, as the City states it: Burnaby's 2026 residential utility notice covers annual water, annual sewer use, a cross-connection device charge where applicable and a residential garbage toter fee; the detached single-family dwelling water charge is $652.33, rates carry a 5% discount if paid by the due date, and for single-family homes sewer is billed as a sewer parcel tax on the property tax notice. Buckingham Heights' established lots sit inside that City serviced system on the City's wording; servicing for any single parcel is confirmed with the City.

ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR parcel in Buckingham Heights is confirmed; no ALR percentage split is stated. ALR status is a property-specific check in the Agricultural Land Commission's ALR Property and Map Finder, not verified lot by lot here.

Flood / hazard position: no floodplain designation for Buckingham Heights' residential streets was confirmed in the sources read; the lakeshore at the sub-area's north-west edge is the wet edge, and parcel-level hazard status is a property-specific check: Not verified for individual lots.

Market context, labelled correctly: Burnaby IS a SnapStats-covered community; SnapStats has NO land category. September 2026 context only, never land figures: Buckingham Heights sub-area detached inventory 12 / solds 0 and "Condos & Townhomes" combined 0 / 0; Burnaby community detached median $1,825,000 and "Condos & Townhomes" combined median $686,000. Sub-area medians are not verified (community level only).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Buckingham Heights

items.t: Zoning — Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026, No. 14815, in effect July 1, 2026: adopted June 9, 2026, it replaced the former Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 1965 (No. 4742) outright — the 1965 bylaw is NOT current and must never be cited for this area.

Heritage diligence: Sperling Avenue fronting Deer Lake Park lies within the Deer Lake Park Heritage Precinct, and heritage-register houses carry heritage review — check the register and the precinct before planning a rebuild or subdivision on a park-fronting lot.

Bare-land strata rules (the BC strata block — stated for the form; no Buckingham Heights plan is verified): Form B diligence (fees, amounts owed, levies, CRF balance, insurance summary; provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions (younger spouse/partner, caregivers, legacy residents, defined children); a listing's "45+" line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Buckingham Heights ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR. Check the parcel on ALC mapping before applying any of this.

Burnaby replaced its zoning bylaw and its OCP within seven months: the Burnaby 2050 OCP was adopted December 9, 2025 and takes precedence over older community-plan maps, and the Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815) took effect July 1, 2026 and repealed the 1965 bylaw — any older guide citing the 1965 zoning bylaw or the 1998 OCP for a Buckingham Heights lot is out of date.

faq.q: Can I buy a condo in Buckingham Heights?

faq.a: Possibly as small multiplexes: Burnaby's R1 SSMUH district allows 3–4 units on standard lots (6 near frequent transit) and lots with two or more primary units may be stratified. No completed named strata complex inside the sub-area was confirmed: Not confirmed.
faq.q: Could new strata product appear here?

faq.a: Yes — Form B on resale, the 10% minimum CRF contribution, and depreciation reports for stratas with five or more lots; a strata of four or fewer lots is exempt from the depreciation-report requirement.
faq.q: If I buy a stratified multiplex unit, do the strata rules still apply?

faq.a: No — long-term rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable anywhere in BC since November 24, 2022; any "rentals not allowed" line is void. Short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw.
faq.q: Can a strata here stop me renting my unit out long-term?
